Zinzi, a beloved doxie girl, had emergency back surgery on Thursday, November 10th, to alleviate compression in her spine that caused her to lose function in her hind legs. Zinzi has a condition called Intervertebral Disc Disease (IVDD), which is common in dogs with long spines. It occurs from degeneration and calcification of the discs between the vertebrae in the spine. On Wednesday, November 9th, we noticed Zinzi grunting and showing signs of physical pain which progressed over the day. Toward the end of the night, Zinzi's movements slowed down, and by 11 pm, she could no longer use her back legs to walk. We took her to the vet first thing the following day, but he could not provide the care she needed due to her progressed condition, so he referred us to a veterinary neurologist. We left the vet and drove directly to the neurologist. He diagnosed her with IVDD and recommended immediate surgery to avoid permanent paralysis. Her surgery lasted about 4 hours, during which he removed the hardened calcification in her vertebrae. Thankfully, the surgery went well without complications, and she spent a couple of nights in the hospital so the vets could monitor her closely. Zinzi is home now and on the road to recovery, and we are slowly learning how to navigate life as she regains strength in her back legs. It will take about two weeks or up to three months for her to walk on her own again, but we are ready for the challenge and hope for a speedy recovery. Your donation would cover the cost of the vet visits, CT scan, MRI, surgery, hospitalization, medication and aftercare. We knew it would be expensive, but if you know Zin, you know she's worth whatever it takes to get her back to her usual self. We love Zinzi so much and are so thankful for all of the doctors, vet techs, family, friends and coworkers who have assisted in Zinzi's journey and recovery. Thank you for taking the time to read her story; sharing this link would mean so much to us.

After 2 weeks of the cold not clearing up, we took him to the vet - that’s when they told us that the situation was far more dire than simply a cold - our little dude was suffering from FIP (Feline Infectious Peritonitis). In most cases, FIP is fatal, with a prognosis of only a few weeks, or a few months if we were lucky. Because he is so young, and was an extremely healthy little dude prior to this, he’s a great candidate for an experimental (and extremely effective) treatment. Unfortunately experimental also means expensive... so here we are. Between the medication itself, the supplies for his injections, and the numerous vet visits it’ll take to run blood tests, check out his vitals, etc, we are looking at a hefty bill - one that 3 baristas and a grad student can’t manage on our own. We know money is tight for everyone right now, especially with the holidays right around the corner, and asking for help is hard - but Ricky has brought endless joy to our lives for the last year and a half, and the thought of losing him is unimaginable. He’s the main character of our apartment, a screaming little goblin who demands the attention of everyone in the room. He’s barely 2 and a half, and we’re confident that if we can get him through treatment, we’ll get many more years with him. We appreciate you reading this far, and please know that whatever help you’re able to offer, whether it’s a donation or simply sharing the link, we are so, so appreciative.

We are blessed to be alive to share our story. We, Precious McNeil and Marco Allen, are the parents of five young, spirited children: Kaliyah (11), Chloe (7), Grace (5), Demarco (2) and Demar (8 months). Precious works as a 911 dispatch operator and Marco is employed at the local Lowe's store. Together, we have coached soccer, T-ball and other youth sports teams with Parks and Recreation for more than five years. We are a close-knit family that enjoys being part of and contributing to our small, rural community. This time last week, our thoughts centered on determining the best neighborhood trick-or-treat routes for our children and their cousins. Two days ago, that all changed. Around 2:30 in the morning, our home was consumed by a house fire. Thankfully, our oldest daughter, Kaliyah, awakened in the middle of the night to use the bathroom. When she opened her eyes, she realized something was very wrong: our home was engulfed in thick smoke. Fortunately, a recent fire drill at her school prepared our daughter to act quickly and wisely. Kaliyah covered her nose and mouth with a bandana, crawled to her mother's bed, screamed her name and shook her to wake her up. Together, they made their way into the living room to locate the other sleeping children amidst the smoke. Remembering where they were earlier in the evening, Kaliyah felt around for Demarco and Grace and carried them out of the house to safety. Precious, Marco and their youngest child followed. Shortly after, when Precious asked about Chloe, without hesitation, Kaliyah ran back into the house to save her sister. We're stunned and emotional. No words can fully express how thankful we are for Kaliyah's bravery. Her courage and selflessness saved not 1, not 2, not 3, not 4, not 5, not 6, but 7 lives. She is our forever hero. The fire destroyed most of our material possessions, and now our young family is forced to start over, from identifying a new home to ensuring our children have their daily needs met. We welcome any level of support as we work to get back on our feet. From the bottom of our grateful hearts, we thank you for reading our story and helping us to celebrate Kaliyah.

My sister and I are posting this GoFundMe for my sister, Vicki, in Daytona Beach Shores, Florida. As many of you know, Hurricane Ian left a path of devastation throughout most of Florida 4 weeks ago. This is one of the biggest storms in Florida history. Many people were left homeless and with nothing. Some losing their lives. One of those people who will soon be without a home is my sister, Vicki Schmand. While she has held out hope that her complex will be spared, that doesn’t appear to be. She lives on Daytona Beach Shores. She watched as this storm did not move for up to 8 hours, gaining momentum as it sat. She has never seen a storm this big. She had taken all precautions that were needed. Vicki is 65 and her income is social security disability. She has lived in her apartment for 12 years. And in Florida for 17. She had established herself there. She had her two dogs, Shrek and Fiona, and her two cats, Calvin and Hobbs. She was, and has been, comfortable and had no plans to move. When this storm hit, it tore a roof off the lower section of the complex. This, in turn, ripped the power lines from the building. She has had no power since the date of the storm. About a month now. There was a thought of connecting temporarily, but there was too much damage inside from extreme winds and rain that came in sideways and under the boards on the windows. This ruined her queen size bed (mattress and boxspring), furniture and carpeting she had, plus other items. This is where she is at. The insurance company would not go for a temporary hookup to the pole. She has done what she could to stay. She has been in contact with FEMA repeatedly. With that said, this is where she is at. Her dogs, Shrek and Fiona, are 18 years old. They have lived a very good and long life. Shrek has congestive heart. She cannot keep him as cool as he needs and had to make the very hard decision to have a vet come in and euthanize. Fiona also has some health issues. And she cannot, in Fiona’s best interest, leave her without her brother. She knows it’s time. This has been the hardest thing she has ever done. As far as a home is concerned...she has many people looking for a camper or trailer that she can stay in temporarily. FEMA has gathered up most of those for the many displaced people. Rents have hit the roof and they are not cheap. She needs to stay within her means. She feels this may be the best decision. There doesn’t seem to be anything else popping up and without AC or power, the heat is becoming unbearable. Recently she has looked at getting a camper and this is the most feasible decision. Where she lost all furniture, these are already set up. One has come up and she would just need the little asked for to complete a purchase. It would be hers and paid for. She also has a place to set it up more inland with a friend. This is family, and this is also an immediate and emergent issue. She has her two cats who are her main concern. So we have set up this fund to help. She has been asked by multiple people where the GoFundMe is so they can help. She told me that the waiting and not knowing what she will do is probably the worst. She sits and thinks and there are no answers. And we all know that that is one of the hardest things. Waiting to see if there is a fix or if there is another shoe dropping. She is stressed, she is tired, and she worries. And we thought this will help alleviate that in at least a small way. We have set a goal. And it is not astronomical and she would not ask for more than she needs. This will help get a camper that is decent sized. To cover two questions people seem to have: 1. She had her two dogs put down. How could she afford that? My husband and I gave her that money. It’s not cheap to have a vet come and do this. We covered it as she had no other choice. 2. How come she did not evacuate when told? Well, they were never informed. It was listed as a tropical storm, and the town has been through many with no real issues. It was not until it came across the state and too late that anyone realized that was not the case. There was no evacuation, and at that point, the bridges got shut down to the peninsula. So everyone in town hunkered down, took precautions, she had all the tenants clear anything out they had outside and boarded windows. It could not have been known that this storm would sit and spin and gain the power it did over Daytona Beach Shores. It was decided by contractors doing the work in the area that a tornado had spun off from the storm just sitting, and that is what did the damages they had. So, please read to the bottom for the most current slap in the face. Vicki is trying to get it straightened out. But needs FEMA to see the damage. She is the only one left at the apartment complex who has not been seen. Even when they come, they can’t just take care of hers. She has to be by appointment only, so she can't do anything when they go to the other tenants. And most all now are gone. UPDATE TO THIS POST: Vicki was contacted by FEMA. They were to come in Saturday, October 15th, and do the inspection. They did not show. She finally got through to them yesterday and they rescheduled for Tuesday ,October 18th. That was great to hear. HOWEVER: she received a text from FEMA and they said to check her account for status? Well, she has no status at the moment besides limbo land. So she did. And it stated the inspection was complete...basically found no damage and there will be no funds given!!! She is totally pissed (sorry, there is no other word at the moment). She is on hold with them and the woman on the line said “what?!” and put her through to talk with whomever. BUT...she said if they closed it then she couldn’t do anything. She was going on 21 days of no power. She did, in fact, get in touch with a supervisor who saw all that was in the records and could not believe how basically botched up it got for no reason. There was no proof of anything they had said. So, she was put back in the system. Again, taking more time to hurry up and wait. SECOND UPDATE: An inspector finally came on Friday, October 21st. She stated her place was a complete loss and filed it as needing all new furniture, miscellaneous, and the funds to move that FEMA allocates. However, when she again checked the status, it stated that she refused the relocation funds, which she did not. She again calls the supervisor, who clearly saw the report that she needed it and, again, had no idea why it was not included and omitted as refused. She was told to FAX her appeal with that information on Monday morning immediately. And she did this. Now she is told it could be another month before she sees that funding. She has now been a month without electric. She would love to have her own place again and be in it for Thanksgiving. And have power once again. Getting the camper, she would own it, and it would show something she has instead of renting for crazy money and not having anything to show. So if you can, please donate to help her out. Every little bit will help. I will update this as she learns more of what is going on. And Please...share...share...share.

El, es Orlando Guerra, nuestro amigo y hermano de la vida “Orlando Bemba”, padre de Nicole (17) y José Leonardo (13), esposo de Lyana Salazar, residenciados en la ciudad de Weston, FL en USA. Orlando, nuestro campeón, se encuentra desde hace un tiempo, pasando por una muy delicada situación de salud y esta necesitando de nuestro apoyo y asistencia. Desde el mes de Enero del 2021, contrajo el virus del COVID; y desde entonces y como consecuencia de ello, ha venido padeciendo de un proceso de Fibrosis Pulmonar, el cual está siendo tratado en el Cleveland Clínic, en la División de Pulmonologia, sin embargo, a pesar de todos los esfuerzos realizados por sus médicos, sus pulmones se han ido deteriorando, y; en consecuencia, han ido disminuyendo su capacidad de oxígeno. En virtud de esta situación, sus doctores concluyeron que Orlando NECESITA UN TRASPLANTE DE AMBOS PULMONES y deciden remitirlo en el Mes de Mayo de este año a la Unidad de TRASPLANTE del Jackson Hospital de la Universidad de Miami. El día 14 de Octubre del presente año, Orlando recibió la llamada del Jackson Hospital en la que se le informaba que después de la evaluación de su caso y de revisar los resultados de todos los respectivos exámenes médicos realizados que dicha solicitud era APROBADA. En estos momentos, se encuentra ya incluido en la Lista de Trasplantes, él junto a su familia se encuentran a la espera de la llamada para la intervención quirúrgica. Con la Fe puesta en la Gracia de Dios y de la bendición de José Gregorio Hernandez, todos oramos para que nuestro campeón salga adelante en esta delicada situación. En virtud de todo lo anterior, y entendiendo la trascendencia de esta delicada operación y de todo su proceso de recuperación post operatorio y; más allá aún, todo su proceso de rehabilitación y el prolongado periodo que este conlleva sin tener la posibilidad ni capacidad para poder trabajar, es que hemos tomado esta iniciativa de apoyo y poder asistir a nuestro amigo y hermano junto a su familia. En este sentido, queremos intentar lograr cubrir todos los gastos del proceso post operatorio, de rehabilitación y de todos los demás gastos que ocurran dentro de estas etapas del proceso y hasta lograr su total y completa recuperación. Para poder lograr esto, hemos tomado la iniciativa de crear esta campaña para recaudar la cantidad de $50,000.00, lo que nos suponemos que es un año entero de recuperación, rehabilitación y de otros gastos elementales y vitales en su vida diaria y en la de los miembros de su familia, y de esta manera, poder llevar una vida menos complicada durante este delicado periodo de recuperación. Nosotros, Benedetto Mazzucco, Nelson Nicoloso y Luis Eduardo Gonsalves, junto a su familia, somos los organizadores de la presente campaña y; en virtud de ello, nos hacemos responsables por los aportes y donaciones realizadas para ayudar a nuestro querido hermano “Bemba” y a su familia ha superar este gran reto que les ha presentado la vida. Gracias a todos por su apoyo ... ORLANDO, TODOS ESTAMOS CONTIGO!!! Iremos compartiendo con todos ustedes cada novedad que acontezca. Y, por favor, no duden en ponerse en contacto con cualquiera de nosotros para cualquier pregunta e información, a través de las siguientes vías: Benedetto Mazzucco: Nelson Nicoloso: Luis Eduardo Gonsalves: NOTA URGENTE: EN ESTOS INSTANTES, EN EL QUE ME ENCUENTRO REDACTANDO EL PRESENTE ESCRITO; ORLANDO, ACABA DE RECIBIR LA LLAMADA DEL JACKSON HOSPITAL PARA INGRASARLO PARA PREPARARLO PARA LA OPERACION!!!

My name is Paul Engle, And I have taken it upon myself to help a fellow Seattle based rider who is in deep need. I have become friends through our amazing community with Will Altieri for a few months now. We have bonded on all things Unicycles and especially the Monster Pro. He has been a solid human being who has never asked for a thing and has been a positive force in the world. I have had to convince him to let me create this Fund for him and his family. Below is his story on what he is going through and what happened to him. We have a large community, and perhaps we can rise up and help the Altieri Family. Lets Go! Here’s What Happened “Its’s my wife, son and I, and I'm the sole provider for our household. I work as the service manager for a company and now I'm being told that I won't be able to start attempting to bear any weight on my leg for 3-6 months after my second surgery. That's bed rest for around half a year. This has cost me my Job and the ability to provide for my family. I was riding my EUC to Starbucks as I do every single day to get my wife and I coffee while on lunch break. Around 4 minutes into the ride, I notice a chemical smell and seen some smoke. I dismissed it as I was on a busy road and sometimes smoke comes from below. Not even 10 seconds later, my temperature on the app was through the roof and my pants were melting. Literally melting. The app said I was going 72mph! when I obviously was nowhere close. Something went VERY wrong. I couldn't stop, could do anything as it cutout and threw me across 3 lanes of traffic, I slid to a stop over a hundred feet from where the initial incident occurred. When I got up, my leg immediately buckled halfway between my ankle and knee. My bone came out of my skin in 3 places. I fell to the ground and became delirious. The fire department arrived on scene as a police officer was trying to extinguish the wheels fire. They could not find a pulse in my foot at all. It was going cold. They immediately cut off the dual axis protectors and did an on-scene emergency reduction. After a bit, they confirmed minor blood flow restoration and placed it into an air cast. I was placed into the c-spine brace as my spine was severely bruised. I had decreased breath sounds in my left lung. I was taken to Harborview Medical Center (a level 1 trauma center) they lost the pulse in my foot again. They immediately began the more extensive trauma workup and when they cleared my c-spine, they then went for an emergency reduction after confirming the severe injury with x-rays and a CT Scan. The medical names for the injuries are open tibia and fibula fractures. My bones are so severely broken that my leg was shorter as the bones shifted upwards towards my knee. They pulled down extremely hard and began manipulating it. This took 30-35 minutes. Once blood flow was positively restored and they confirmed proper capillary refill - I was sent to surgery. However, surgery failed as the initial damage was too much. The swelling was too bad. They had no way to put my skin back together if they kept at it. So they opted for an external fixator with 5 pins. Two in my foot (heel and the ankle) and then 3 higher up in the leg. I was in the hospital for 5 days. Surgery cannot happen until at least November 3rd. After surgery, I will be in the hospital for around 3 weeks. I currently have no movement in my toes or foot. I can feel very few things but what I do feel, is an intense burning pain. Work is not providing assistance and my apartment building understands the issue - but they cannot let rent go unpaid. The medications cost me an additional $72 per week and I have to purchase refills every week of a different lifesaving medication that I have to be on for 6 weeks which is a blood thinning shot. Each refill is $62 per week. We now have to pay rent, bills, medical transports, medications and somehow still buy groceries when I am not even able to put my foot to the ground for 3-6 months after my next surgery. I don’t know what to do" That’s It Can we Rise up and help the Altieri Family? When I blew my knee out years ago I didn’t have insurance and I had to start a gofundme myself in order to afford it. If it hadn’t been for that help, I would not have been able to get use of my knee back and I definitely wouldn’t be riding today. So let’s join as a community and see what we can really make happen.

Like other people from my minority we had to escape to the mountain since my city was completely occupied by ISIS except the mountain. My family, and I had to escape to the mountain. We survived there for nine days without any food and water, or anything we owned. We were eating leaves and drinking the rainwater stored in caves. It was truly an unfortunate situation. I observed heartbreaking scenes, I saw friends and relatives being killed, dying of thirst and starvation, people crying, frightened by the bullet shots over us. We were close to losing the hope to continue in life, until we escaped to northern Iraq. We were kept in plastic tents for more than 5 years and it has been like that since then. My home and most of my hometown were destroyed. Specifically, the house that my parents worked on building their lives, was bombed and left to ashes during the occupation. After five years, we went back to our city in the hopes that our government would rebuild it. We were residing in a house that did not belong to us because the previous owners had left Iraq. As a result, after the city's situation began to improve and numerous organisations began to visit, people began renting out the remaining houses. As a result, the owner asked my family to leave the home and granted them two months to do so, a while ago. Meaning, my family and I are at a loss as to what to do since we have nowhere else to live. Especially since living in tents would be extremely difficult due to the incoming harsh winter in the north of Iraq. But I didn't give up. I made a pledge to my parents, who are both ill in Iraq and are unable to work, to finish my studies and work hard to achieve their dreams. I started working the maximum number of hours on campus, despite the fact that it is interfering with my studies since I do not have excellent mental health, but I am doing everything I can to help them, and it is not working. On Friday, October 28, 2022 my 70-year-old dad, Alan Ash, was a victim of a high-speed, head-on collision just outside of Deming, New Mexico. He is my hero and my rock and I am beyond grateful that he survived. Due to his injuries, he is facing an indeterminate amount of time off of work from his beloved profession as a Stonemason. Dad lives and works on the road, so this devastating event - which totaled both his truck and travel trailer - has also left him homeless and 1600 miles from home base in Oregon. As we have been navigating the challenges of this tragic situation, it has become apparent that his immediate need is financial support. The financial impacts of losing both vehicles is especially difficult. Dad had just put a brand-new, factory-remanufactured, 12-valve Cummins engine into his ‘98 Dodge Ram 4x4 flatbed. He also recently bought a new-to-him 2018 Jayco Jay Flight Baja Edition travel trailer. This was his first extended trip after both of these upgrades. Dad is largely self-employed and I have created this fundraiser to help provide him with financial stability that he needs to heal, regain his independence and resume his passion and livelihood as a Stonemason. Donations will be used towards these needs: A roof over his head to physically and emotionally recover. This may include temporary shelter and/or travel arrangements to be closer to family who can provide care and support. The ultimate goal is to eventually replace his travel trailer to ensure he has permanent shelter. Time away from work to heal physically and emotionally, and to ensure all medical needs are accessible to him. A vehicle - replacing his truck with one that is capable of carrying his work tools and hauling a travel trailer is the ultimate goal. In the meantime he will need some form of transportation. Storage for his salvageable personal effects and undamaged work tools. Replacing his damaged personal effects. Asking for financial help is humbling and I do not take lightly making this request, especially during the instability of the current economic climate. Any amount you can donate would mean a lot. If you are unable to donate, just sharing this GoFundMe to reach more people would be helpful. More About Alan Ash, Stonemason What makes my dad vibrant is his passion as a Stonemason. Over the last 40 years, he has become a well-respected expert and teacher in the historical restoration and preservation of stonework. He is passionate about passing his knowledge of this dying art form on to younger generations to preserve our nation’s indigenous and modern stonework with historical accuracy. If you have been to Joshua Tree National Park, Shenandoah National Park, Lassen National Monument, Sheldon National Wildlife Refuge or Saguaro National Park you may have unknowingly seen his work and influence. He has worked on over 100 buildings on the National Register of Historic Places, within 15 Oregon State parks, at US Fish and Wildlife Service locations, on BLM historical properties and more - this list is just the tip of the iceberg. On private properties in Virginia’s Western Highlands and in Western Oregon, Dad has built hundreds of rock walls, dozens of stone chimneys and many pieces of stone art. Dad’s lifestyle is intensely physically active. In late 2021, one job required a daily 5-mile hike into the job site and the same hike out again at the end of a physically demanding workday. He is an incredible gardener and a lifelong musician. He is also the biggest nature lover - he regularly sends me sunset photos from incredibly remote areas. Most importantly to me, he is the very best dad and grandpa that anyone could ask for. I would be so thankful for any amount of money that you can donate, for sharing this fundraiser with others and also for any positive energy you can send dad’s way. With gratitude, Hollie Ash

If the animals die, the Amboseli Maasai starve. And right now, they are staving. The market for selling livestock has crashed because people are selling their animals before they die to buy food (maize, rice, beans), creating a glut of animals for sale. William said that a cow that used to sell for 40,000 Kenyan shillings (about $350) no sells for 8,000 Kenyan shillings (about $65). Trying to get a dying cow to stand up Cow partially eaten by hyenas Baby sheep This giraffe died beside the Amboseli school Zebra Cape buffalo Baboon Wildebeest Impala Warthog They need money to buy hay for their animals. William did not ask me for money. I have sent them money and will continue to do so, but their clan needs more help than I can provide. I hope you can find it in your heart to help the Amboseli Maasai through this crisis Mungo akubariki (Swahili: “God Bless You”)

Hola soy Juliennys, pero las personas que me aman me llaman “Juli” o “Julo”. Y hoy quiero contarles lo que ha sido mi historia en retrospectiva. Hace 6 meses vivía una vida perfecta, y digo perfecta porque la perfección existe en miles de momentos que damos por sentado, y que no apreciamos ni valoramos. En marzo acudo a mi ginecólogo por control, me mando a hacer unos exámenes de rutina, y aunque observa mis valores un poco alterados me dice que es anemia, que no tengo que preocuparme, me recetó unas vitaminas y así hice. Luego en agosto me siento una pelota en el cuello, y acudo a un internista donde me dice que era un ganglio inflamado, me manda a hacer una hematologia especial y nuevamente coincide con mi doctor anterior y me dice que es una anemia, el tratamiento esta vez fueron sesiones de suero terapia (una semanal). Sin embargo yo sentía algo raro en mi, me sentía siempre cansada, agotada, tenía el alrededor del iris amarillo, dolores de cabeza, y muchas cosas que me decían que algo no estaba bien. No fue hasta el 16 de septiembre que empecé con un dolor muy grave en el lumbar, empecé a realizarme más y más exámenes, acudir a doctores y lo que se veía a simple vista era que tenía la hemoglobina baja, leucocitos bajos y linfocitos altos. Las cosas iban empeorando y yo seguía sin diagnóstico, sin saber que tenía o que me pasaba. Decidí viajar a Houston, donde vive mi familia, y aquí me dieron un diagnóstico que nadie quiere escuchar, Leucemia Mieloide Aguda... Resultados del aspirado de médula, dando como resultado Leucemia Ya hospitalizada y preparada para empezar con mis quimioterapias, me diagnostican un coágulo de sangre en el pulmón izquierdo, y además, a través de más exámenes, los doctores encontraron que mi corazón no está funcionando bien.. Resultado D Dimer, donde se ve que mi corazón no está trabajando bien Actualmente me tienen con los siguientes medicamentos hasta estabilizarme y poder empezar finalmente con la quimioterapia: -Antibióticos: (para evitar cualquier tipo de infección) Acyclovir Ciprofloxacin Fluconazol -Anticoagulante: (inyecciones dos veces al día en el abdomen) Enoxaparin (lovenox) -Corazón: Lisinopril Metoprolol tartrate En este proceso, entendí que para Dios no hay imposibles, y si su voluntad fue esa, yo tenía que aceptarla y empezar a hacerle frente con fé y confianza en él. Entendí que para sanar tengo que perdonar y perdonarme, pues no sabía lo bendecida y valiosa que era mi vida. Entendí que tengo que agradecer todo lo hermoso que uno da por sentado en esta vida: una familia y un esposo que me ama, amigos incondicionales que me apoyan en absolutamente todo, personas hermosas que me han acompañado siempre, y muchas cosas más que quizás antes no veía. Pero lo más importante en estos momentos es que entendí que mi mayor deseo es VIVIR, vivir una vida sana, alrededor de todas las personas que me aman, me quieren, me estiman y me valoran, que DESEO formar una familia, tener un hogar, disfrutar de todas las pequeñas cosas que me regala la vida. Por eso hoy acudo a ti, con el corazón en la mano, para pedirte que me ayudes. Les confieso que jamas imaginé que me tocaría estar de este lado, cómo la paciente que necesita salvar su vida. Pero así es la vida, yo se que esta enfermedad no me va a vencer, yo decidí pelear esta batalla, y se que junto a Dios todo es posible. Les prometo ser fuerte, les prometo que si caigo me volveré a levantar todas las veces que sean necesarias, yo seguiré luchando hasta ganar esta guerra, y empezar una nueva vida, sana y libre de Cáncer.. ...Mi historia continúa, y aquí estoy para ponerte al día en el avance que he tenido hasta ahora. Estoy tan agradecida con Dios y todos los que me han acompañado en este viaje llamado Leucemia. Al fin puedo decir ¡Estoy en remisión! Si bien la guerra continúa, estar en remisión me hace sentir esperanzada. Queda camino por recorrer ya que mi leucemia es de riesgo medio, lo que lleva a los especialistas a remitirme a un transplante de médula ósea. En tanto llega el momento debo seguir recibiendo quimios de consolidación. Por lo tanto sigo necesitando de su ayuda para poder costear todos los gastos que genera esta enfermedad. ¡Gracias! gracias por mantenerte ahí, gracias por tus palabras de aliento, Gracias por tu granito de arena, gracias infinitas. ——— English ———— Hi, I'm Juliennys, but people who love me call me “Juli” or “Julo”. And today I want to tell you what my story has been in retrospect. 6 months ago I was living a perfect life, and I say perfect because perfection exists in thousands of moments that we take for granted and that we do not appreciate or value. In March I went to my gynecologist for control, he sent me to do some routine exams, and although he sees my values a little altered, he tells me that it is anemia and that I don't have to worry about it, and he prescribed me some vitamins. Then in August, I felt a lump in my neck, I went to an internist doctor, where he tells me it was a swollen lymph node, he sends me to do special hematology and again he agrees with my previous doctor and tells me that it is anemia. The treatment at that time was to do a serum therapy sessions (once weekly). However, I felt something strange in me, I always felt tired, and exhausted, multiples headaches, my body at that time was telling me that something was not right. It was not until September 16 that I began with a very serious pain in my lower back, I began to perform more and more tests, and go to different doctors and the only thing they seen was that I had low hemoglobin, low leukocytes, and high lymphocytes. Things were getting worse and I still hadn't been diagnose, not knowing what I had or what was wrong with me. I decided to travel to Houston, where my family lives, and here they gave me a diagnosis that nobody wants to hear, Acute Myeloid Leukemia. Already hospitalized and ready to start my chemotherapies, they find out that I have a blood clot in my left lung, and furthermore, through more tests, the doctors found that my heart is not working well. Currently they have me on the following medications until I stabilize and finally start chemotherapy: -Antibiotics: (to avoid any type of infection) acyclovir, Ciprofloxacin, fluconazole -Anticoagulant: (injections twice a day in the abdomen) Enoxaparin (lovenox) -Heart: Lisinopril, metoprolol tartrate In this process, I understood that nothing is impossible for God, and if this was his will, I had to accept it and begin to face it with faith and trust in him. I understood that to heal I have to forgive and forgive myself, because I did not know how blessed and valuable my life was. I understood that I have to thank all the beautiful things that I take for granted in my life: a family and a husband who love me, unconditional friends who support me in absolutely everything, beautiful people who have always accompanied me, and many more things than I didn't realize before. But the most important thing at this momento is that I understood that my greatest desire is to LIVE, to live a healthy life, surrounded by all the people who love me, take care of me, value me, that I WANT to form a family, have a home, enjoy all the little things that life gives me. That's why today I come to you, with my heart in my hand, to ask you to help me. I confess that I never imagined that I would have to be on this side, as the patient who needs to save her life. But that's life, I know that this disease will not defeat me, I decided to fight this battle, and I know that with God everything is possible. I promise to be strong, I promise that if I fall I will get up again as many times as necessary, I will continue fighting until I win this war, and start a new life, healthy and free of Cancer.. ...My story continues, and here I am to update you on the progress I've had so far. I am so grateful to God and to everyone who have been with me on this journey called Leukemia. Finally I can say I'm in remission! Even though the war continues, being in remission makes me feel hopeful. There is a long way to go because my leukemia is medium risk, which leads the specialists to refer me for a bone marrow transplant. Until the time comes, I must continue receiving consolidation chemo. Therefore, I still need your help to be able to pay for all the expenses that this disease generates. Thanks! Thank you for staying with me, thank you for your words of encouragement, thank you infinitely.

Hello, my name is Kim and this is my 6 year old border collie, Booker. On 11/11, Booker had to have emergent surgery to remove what the vet thought was a foreign body object. Once in surgery, I received a call that this was not a foreign body object, but in fact a mass. A mass that neither vet had ever seen nor could identify. I was asked if I wanted to biopsy the mass, have them remove it, or do nothing. I elected to have them biopsy it and try to remove it. I was told this mass had an adhesion to the colon which is Very BadTM️ and they would not be able to remove it, a specialist would have to do that. I still wanted them to proceed with the biopsy. I got a second call that the biopsy was very difficult to obtain, Booker began to rupture, do I want them to continue or should my dog be euthanized on the table? I begged them to please try to stop the bleeding and keep my dog alive. They were able to get the bleeding under control, but the vet said it was very difficult to reconnect the edges where the biopsy was taken from. Booker still has a chance of his intestines opening back up and bleeding out internally. We were sent home while Booker was still waking up from anesthesia and it was a rough night. We ended up at the emergency vet’s office on Saturday 11/12 due to Booker pulling some staples from his incision, possible dehydration, and overall monitoring. He came home Sunday 11/13 and was still touch and go overnight. He finally started eating the evening of 11/13 and has been eating since. One of the original vet’s biggest worries was him not eating and not getting his intestines moving properly. We seem to be on the right track but still have a long ways to go. We are awaiting biopsy results and from there, will need to see a specialist regarding... whatever this mass is. Funds from here will be used to help pay for the initial surgery and emergency vet. A bulk of the funds will go towards the specialist he will need that my vet estimated to cost “an astronomical amount.” My Bookie boy was previously healthy until this happened. He enjoyed his walks, going to the park, eating and treats, cuddling his favorite avocado toy, his cat buddy Salad, and growling at the other two dogs if they were having too much fun without him. We had gone to the vet less than a month prior for his annual check up, they did not notice anything wrong with him at that time. I think my boy still has a lot of life left to live. Anything will help us in this unexpected mess. Monetary donations of any size will be forever appreciated, but sharing or even just giving Booker a thought/prayer/vibe for successful recovery are also forever appreciated. Thank you so much for reading this.

Well, it looks like I'm out of commission for quite a while. Here's the story in case you haven't heard it... On Sunday, Oct. 30, 2022, I had a speed-flying accident at Soboba Flight Park in Southern California. It was my first time flying from this particular launch point, and everything was simply gorgeous and amazing until I made a misjudgment in my proximity to the ground. I took it too low and impacted the terrain at about 40 mph. I tumbled downhill through rocks, dirt, and tumbleweed for probably 40-50 feet. Luckily, where I ended up was right above the Kobata trail just as a Kobata was on its way up! People were there within 30 seconds to help. They had to helicopter me down to the ambulance, and the whole process took a couple of hours. Then I had a 30-minute ride to the hospital where they brought me into the trauma unit and did x-rays immediately. I burst my L4 and had a broken nerve. I had to be completely flat on my back for 48 hours. They did surgery two days later and thankfully everything went fine, although apparently, I should be dead. They put a cage in for my L4 and rods between the L3 to L4 and L4 to L5. On Friday, Nov. 4, I was transferred out of the ICU and I have started PT. Just today I was [thankfully] approved for Medi-Cal, which should cover most or all of the medical costs. I'll be moving to an acute rehab facility hopefully tomorrow, but the insurance only covers rehab centers in this area, which means I won't be home for a while. It's been the most excruciating and miserable experience of my life, and recovery is going to continue to be a physical and emotional struggle. But I have learned from it. And maybe eventually I'll share my story so others won't make the same dumbass mistake I did, nearly ending my life. Thanks to my rock, Blane Moler, for putting up with my unrelenting tears, profanity breakouts, and driving in the horrid SoCal traffic twice a day to be by my side. And to my beyond-supportive family who is always there for me. And to our amazing friend, Roger Hoffman, for taking care of our fur babies back in Lodi. And to the staff of Riverside University Health System Medical and Surgical Center. And to everyone else who has been so supportive. I'm miserable right now but also happy to be alive! I have no idea when I'll be able to work again (hence this post). I freaking hate asking for monetary help, but this is one of those blows that life sends, leaving you without many choices. Thank you SO MUCH to everyone who has reached out. I can't keep up with all the messages, but know they mean a lot.

This is Crystal Jones. Many people around Atlanta know her as grandmother. What follows is an opportunity for the community to rally around a woman that does so much for so many, and now needs our support in return. Crystal is a modern-day Mary Poppins. She might show up to watch your kids for the night with a bounce house. On weekends, she drives around a 15-passenger van, picks up a gaggle of kids and takes them out on incredible day-long adventures. They return home tired, fed, and so happy. Their parents have had a full day to themselves. Crystal provides the most exceptional care for children all over metro Atlanta, and she will tell you it's because she raised 4 kids on her own and she wants parents to feel supported in ways she never did. Her smile is infectious and her warmth can be felt at 200 yards. She manages to provide support for so many families, and she wants to start a business (the website is almost finished!). But when she goes home from caring for others' kids, she cares for two adult children with disabilities under the direst of circumstances. Crystal is the most enterprising, entrepreneurial person you will ever meet, but she is underwater caring for her sons and dealing with a medical system and housing system that keep shutting them out. She has worked for decades to find solutions, to work the systems. But they're just not working for her. That's where we come in. 1. Steaven Crystal's adult son Steaven was diagnosed with schizophrenia as a teenager. It has taken years to find the right combination of medicines that help him be comfortable and communicative (such as a monthly shot of Invega). But Georgia Medicare has declined to cover that medication. Without insurance, it's $1,200 a month. That's almost half of the family's income. Without the medication, Steaven's condition becomes severe and he suffers tremendously, sometimes wanders off. Recently, during a particularly bad episode, he was arrested. The danger of mental illness for young Black men is exponentially greater because police often see them as a threat. Steaven's medicine is critical for his life, his safety, and the peace and safety of his family. One of the only ways Crystal can get support for Steaven is when his condition is severe enough that he can be committed to a county hospital. That triggers some emergency support that only lasts a few weeks after he is hospitalized. It's traumatic for Steaven and for Crystal. 2. Ronald Meanwhile, Crystal is also caring for her other adult son, Ronald, who was paralyzed several years ago. Their home is not wheelchair accessible, and Crystal has to move her son in and out of the bathroom on a wheeled desk chair in order to fit through the door. While she has sufficient income and savings to afford a better apartment or even a down payment on a house, because she is self-employed she hasn't been able to get a loan or provide sufficient income verification to find an accessible three-bedroom rental. They have been taken advantage of by an unethical landlord who has refused to repair their hot water. The family has been living without running hot water for more than four months. Crystal's dream is to live in a quiet place with lots of woods where she and her sons can enjoy the outdoors. She wants peace and calm for Steaven. She wants Ronald to be able to access the bathroom on his own (and he would like that, too!) We are raising funds: To underwrite Steaven's medication so he can get stable and he and Crystal can work on a plan together for his long term care To pay enough advance rent that the family can move to an accessible apartment We are also looking for an attorney who may be able to help with Steaven's case If you can lend a hand navigating the Medicare system for mental health in Georgia (or you know another place in the Southeast where they can find better care), if you have connections to a pro-bono attorney or better housing for this family, please reach out. Thank you!

This is my sweet boy, Squash Hammy Croissant. Yesterday morning, while playing with his favorite toys, Squash stopped to lay down and started showing signs he wasn’t feeling good. An otherwise healthy kitty - up to date on his vaccines and check-ups, and a happy, active boy - his symptoms were worrisome and within a couple of minutes he was quickly declining. We headed to the vets for an emergency appointment, but when Squash was becoming unresponsive and struggling to breathe, we were transferred to a bigger emergency animal hospital nearby, where the doctor gave us the worst kind of news: Squash is battling heart failure. Taken into immediate treatment - oxygen, IVs, and close monitoring - the doctor noted Squash’s temperature was rapidly decreasing and an examination revealed a masked heart disease, impacting his ability to breathe and leaving his lungs filled with fluid. The first priority was getting Squash’s body stabilized again, which the doctor compassionately warned may not be a possible outcome. In that case, we would have to say a very unexpected and oh too soon goodbye. We decided to continue the treatments for the recommended 24-48 hours and then go from there, all while keeping a close watch on Squash and making sure his healing and comfort were the main focus of every decision. After spending the night at the hospital, Squash was seen by a cardiologist this morning to assess his condition. He has a type of heart disease that will need additional care, but once stabilized in the hospital for a few days of treatment, he has the hope of returning home to his favorite things, soaking in sun puddles, and being surrounded by his family. And as of this afternoon, Squash is already responding to treatment - his temperature is rising out of hypothermia, he is becoming more responsive, and he is slowly coming back to us. He is still on oxygen while the doctors are working to strengthen his breathing and get the remaining fluid out of his lungs, but we got the best gift we could ask for today: hope. With a detailed plan and attentiveness to it, Squash has the hope of not just coming home again, but feeling like himself and enjoying the rest of his days without suffering. Our life together only began earlier this year, and while I’m eternally grateful for each moment we have, I want to make sure Squash has a fighting chance to spend more time doing the things he loves and being around the people who love him. Coming home will also require us to start a careful care routine - including daily medication and regular checkups. Unlike the case for many hospitals for humans, animal hospitals often require payment before treatment - and in the case of an emergency like this, it can be a really terrifying challenge to find the means to pay for treatment, knowing a little one’s life depends on it. Finding a way to afford the treatment when you can’t afford to lose any time. I can’t bear the thought that money would get in the way of Squash getting the care he needs. Right now, the cost of his remaining hospital treatments, medication and outpatient care is estimated to be around $4,000. Asking for money is definitely out of my comfort zone, but for Squash, I want to give him every chance I can. Thank you for hearing our story, sharing, or supporting in any way you can. It means the whole world.

The child you see in the photo above is Doug Nash. Until the spring of 2022, he was an average adolescent. He was outgoing, caring, funny and quite intelligent for his age. He had the typical bumps and bruises, including casts on his wrist and elbow from skateboarding. That all changed on May 22nd. While skateboarding with friends, Doug took a hard fall that left him with multiple facial fractures. With the immediate suspicion of TBI (traumatic brain injury), Doug was airlifted to Harborview Medical center in Seattle while his family hurriedly made the drive to sit by his side. The CT Scan did not show any significant harm to the front of his brain. Within a week, Doug was able to return home to Yakima. Doug and his family would revisit Harborview and also travel to Children's Hospital to monitor his recovery. At the three-month mark, Doug failed all of the benchmarks the surgeons had for him, and his family noticed a continued downward spiral in his overall health and personality. He started to suffer from double vision and a lack of energy and strength and would sometimes sleep for up to 20 hours a day. His health issues required him to enroll in school on a 504 plan, an accommodation allowing him to learn at the pace he needed while pursuing medical assistance. Doug's memory and motor skills started deteriorating further, and he developed nausea and vertigo. On September 20th, he received his first MRI. For months, the medical team believed Doug's troubles had been from the skateboarding fall, meaning the CT Scan should have been sufficient to diagnose his problems and not require the additional examination. The MRI told a different story. They found a large pineal cyst measuring 2.5cm x 1.7cm x 1.0cm in AP. The cyst was pushing his brain both forward and back against his skull. It covers his pineal gland, which controls melatonin levels, affects sleep and helps stabilize one's quality of life, something Doug was severely lacking. Family members started remembering Doug's occasional mentions of headaches or vision problems before his skateboarding accident. This growth may be the root of all his troubles, stemming months before the fall. Once Doug and his family received the diagnosis, the next problem arose. Pineal cystic tumors are challenging to remove and something that Children's Hospital does not offer. Doug's mom Desiree exhausted hours researching the growth and any possible solutions. She found there were only a handful of surgeons in the world willing to operate and attempt to remove the growth and only one that would work on a child. One doctor. She found the contact information she needed in an article about Dr. Infinger at the Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC), sent an email and hoped for a response. Almost immediately, her prayers were answered. Dr. Infinger replied and said she had operated on hundreds of these cysts, but this was the largest she personally had seen. The size of Doug's growth is extremely rare, but the doctor said she would not have replied if she didn't believe she could help. They ordered a second MRI, with contrast this time, a month after his previous one, to examine whether it was continuing to grow or was stable. Doug and his family met with Dr. Infinger via Tele-Medicine Zoom, and were thankfully informed there was little change. Surgery to remove the growth is now set for January 18th, 2023. He will need to arrive a few days before the operation. Once the surgery is complete, the best-case scenario is for Doug to stay in the hospital for 5-7 days. The cyst is so large that once it is removed, Doug will suffer from pain due to a shift in brain pressure that will cause additional headaches and vision problems at the very least. He won't be able to travel for a minimum of two weeks; again, this is the best-case scenario. Thankfully, most of Doug's medical care will be covered by the insurance his parents have. But, the insurance doesn't cover his travel, nor his family's travel, and their need to stay by his side for what is likely three to six weeks. This fundraiser is not to pay specifically for Doug's care, but for his family to accompany him to South Carolina for surgery and recovery. Doug's parents Desiree and Derek, are no longer together and lead separate lives. As you might imagine, any 11-year-old would want both of his parents to be with him as much as possible through this ordeal. Travel, accommodations and meal expenses will add up extremely fast for Doug and his family this winter. Once he returns home, that doesn't mean he is out of the woods. The cyst will be biopsied and hoped to be benign. Even with that best case, he will likely need follow-up and rehabilitative care at Children's Hospital in Seattle. Your generosity will help ensure he receives all the loving support he will need for his recovery. Thank you in advance for reading Doug's story and for any support you are able to offer.

He flipped the kitchen table, threw chairs at me and tried to destroy my phone that had evidence on it of his behavior. Once we escaped to our neighbors, he set the house on fire by putting my clothes on the stove and also set our sectional couch on fire. As we were hiding at the neighbors we saw him exit the house. We called 911 again for the 2nd time because we thought he was coming after us, but instead he sat in a chair in the yard laughing that he destroyed the house. The police arrived and he calmly announced that yes, he set the house on fire and take him to jail and he was trying to kill us all. My children and I watched as our whole life went up in flames. We escaped with only our pajamas on, and no shoes and no coats. The fire marshall and investigators were kind enough to search the house and retrieve a few special items, my son’s pooh bears and my daughters baby blanket and my bible. My bible was the only thing intact with no water damage. We had 2 cats, one was confirmed to be alive as he ran out soaked in water. Sadly, we had no home owners insurance so we have lost everything and have to restart from scratch. Several friends have donated clothing, shoes and some toys for the children. Physically, we are safe and unharmed. Mentally, this is a lot to process. The outpouring of concern, support and love from our neighborhood, schools and community is beyond anything I could imagine during this nightmare. I have reached out to my children’s schools and they are setting up gift card drives and clothing closets for us as well as many many messages being sent to me via Facebook. We have access to the Rochester Neighborhood House, food pantry and clothes closet. I will respond to each and every one of you for your kindness and thoughtfulness and outpouring of support for my children and I. My hope is to remain in this community and neighborhood “my village” and have been having many discussions regarding purchasing a “new to us” mobile home. This will be a long, tedious journey that we are now on. Any monies donated will go to helping us secure housing. For now, and indefinitely we are safe at a non-disclosed location for our safety and healing. We are taking it one hour at a time as we come together to share our common grief, anger, confusion and disbelief. I think with the support we will be receiving from neighbors and community the children and I will be well taken care of for daily and personal needs but now, as a single mom, I am left wholly responsible for securing our future. I will be seeking out grants to help secure down payments as needed, but request any monetary donations to help with future housing, and general bills while I am not able to work so I may focus on the healing that my children need, as well as making sure the 2 littles who both have birthdays in the next few weeks, may have good memories for this birthday... because they are kids and they don’t deserve this. My children are talking about everything and I have counselors and support for them set up, but the emotions are too much and we are really struggling. My husband... is currently under arrest at a local hospital awaiting arraignment and transfer being charged with arson, domestic violence and attempted murder. I will update as much as possible and be changing the donation amount as I receive donations, etc., from my community. I wasn’t sure what to set the donation amount as so I will modify it to account for the outpouring of support that is received. Thank you from the bottom of my heart for taking the time to read this, and if you can’t help, please know I appreciate all prayers sent! I want all my neighbors and community members to know that I am trying to keep up with reading your messages and will try to get in contact with you as soon as I can. In the mean time, a friend in the neighborhood is organizing donations that can be dropped off. If you are interested in contacting her directly, you can find her on Facebook at Jammy Allard. If you would feel more comfortable any donations can be arranged for drop off at Rochester Estates main office, McGregor Elementary School or Hart Middle School. Never would I believe I would be living this nightmare, but with the love and outpouring of support for my family from my neighborhood and community I know we will soon arise from these ashes... blessing to you all. (For the safety and sake of the children involved, I found it best not to post photos of them as they are still in the country and are minors.) My mother (Fowsia Musse) was traveling there to see her family for the first time since she left in 1993 at age 12. Upon arrival to Jijiga, my mom was also shot and injured at the airport, and my brother was injured as well. I've been in contact with the Ethiopian and United States Embassy in regard to bringing my family back home and ensuring the safety of my family in Jijiga. Juweria was, and will still continue to be, a well-respected political figure, an excellent mother, and a beautiful soul. Inshallah justice is served in her name. My aunt Juweria will forever be remembered. I love everybody dearly, and my family and I are eternally grateful for all of the support that we have received; Words are not tantamount to the emotions that are being felt at this time. Please pray for the recovery of my family, and for the safety of them as well. ❤️ I want to kindly, sincerely, and viscerally thank everybody who has expressed their sorrow, care, and concern regarding the recent murder of my beloved aunt Juweria Subcis. The resources and security help that my family has received from the United States government & Ethiopian Embassies are immeasurable beyond words. As most people know, my mother’s name is Fowsia Musse. I am Shadia, the eldest daughter of five children in the United States. My mother said she feels extremely blessed and grateful to have people to care for her, her family, and her children. She wanted me to thank you all for being so kind and welcoming toward this extenuating circumstance that has traumatized my family. My mother came to the United States at the age of 13. After waiting for her visa for two years and saving money, my mother was finally able to see her family for the first time in 27 years. Seeing the excitement in her eyes when her sister Juweria came to our home in the United States for the first time & hearing how highly she spoke of her anticipated visit back home spread joy in my family and community, as we all were aware of how much she wanted to see her family and one day return there to visit. Everything my mother did, she always thought of her family back home in Jijiga, and she relentlessly worked upon her arrival to this country out of selfless love and care for those in her life. My mother especially wanted to go home to see her mother, who was recently diagnosed with sarcoma. She had not seen her mother since she was a pre-teenage girl, and words are still not tantamount to the emotions she must've felt when she saw her mother upon her arrival in Addis. Along with my mother, my 14-year-old brother Mubarik and my 8-year-old sister Hawa were on the trip. It was their first time leaving the country, flying, and their first time meeting our family in Ethiopia. Hour by hour, I was receiving updates from my mom as she was packing, cleaning, and preparing for her trip — each update, the smile on her face grew larger. I’ll never forget the day she got her Visa in the mail; The small green document that was the only thing left that she needed to leave and see her family. My mother said that she felt complete. My aunt Juweria Subcis was an MP in the Somali regional state parliament; A member of the Somali Peace Party. Juweria was also a U.S. Mandela Fellow in Washington D.C., and the Human Resources Manager at Oxfam in Ethiopia (an NGO). Juweria, alike my mother, worked hard in her community to serve and educate those that are underprivileged; Whether it was doing groundwork and delivering Covid-19 information, running testing centers, or even traveling the country and region to participate in peace talks about the ongoing political tensions in the area, Juweria was gracious and intentional in her work and efforts. Juweria was indeed the apex and epitome of a true humanitarian. Yesterday morning around 8:00am EST, I got a phone call informing me that Juweria had been killed by security upon arrival to the Jijiga Airport. My mother, brother, and sister had flown in to Jijiga so that they could see her family that was there (her sisters, father, brother, and cousins/aunts/uncles). Juweria was shot and killed. After killing my aunt Juweria, the security officer began to spray bullets across the entirety of the airport, resulting in a myriad of injuries. My mother was also shot and injured, sustaining wounds from two shots in the stomach and hip. My brother was grazed by a bullet in his shoulder, leaving him with stitches. As of 2:00pm EST today, I’ve received word that my mother will have to be flown to the capital city of Addis Ababa to receive proper medical treatment, as she has anemia and lupus. I have been attempting to keep contact with family who is with her, but it has been difficult as everyone is grieving the loss of Juweria and the aftermath as such. The funeral was yesterday morning, and the government has called October 25th 'Black Tuesday' to signify the gravity of Juweria’s passing and how her loss will impact Jijiga and the Somali State forever. Thousands of people around the country of Ethiopia and tens of thousands of people online called for her justice. Juweria leaves behind with her two beautiful children. For security, safety and privacy concern, I will leave them unnamed until further approval. They are two boys that are similar in age to my brother and sister and I cannot imagine the grief and confusion that they are experiencing at this moment. Juweria always expressed how proud she was of them, and would talk about attending their future graduations and seminars. I kindly and sincerely ask for the prayers and positivity wishes for her children. Both of my siblings that are there are currently in the care of my grandmother and aunt. This is their first time in a foreign country, and they do not have their mother with them nor do they know what is going on. They, alike Juweria’s children, are traumatized and afraid, and I pray for their long-term mental health recovery. I have been in contact with the embassies in regard to their safety and return, and luckily I was granted a Visa to go there myself and be excused from college for the time being, but as of now, the bigger details have been left in the air. I created this GoFundMe with the most kind and humble intention of raising money for rehabilitation costs for Juweria’s children, their family back home, and my family in the United States. My mother and brother will need specialized medical treatment and physical therapy, and the three of them together will need to undergo mental health therapy and psychiatric services. It is being reported that my mother has a broken leg and may need further specialized surgery upon her return to the United States in the next few weeks. Juweria’s children will need funding for mental health services, rehabilitation services, and relocation, as Juweria was their only parent in the country, and they must relocate to the appropriate person/area of residency. My grandmother has cancer, and now she will also need to undergo chemotherapy in Nairobi as well as mental health services and therapy, as she lost her second daughter, and her eldest is critically injured upon arrival to the area. For proof or supportive documentation/further inquiry, please feel free to message me for more details and I will gladly and kindly explain to you. The trauma and pain that my mother left 20+ years ago only revisited her on Tuesday October 25th. A trip that was supposed to be the trip of my mother’s dreams quite literally turned into a nightmare in 72 hours. I do not expect everybody to donate, share their prayers, or extend themselves further than they have the means to. I sincerely hope that we are able to look past race and politics, and understand that a mother was taken from us, and another mother was harmed with children involved. I kindly ask that all comments and statements (especially political opinions) are not posted on here, as it would be of utmost disrespect. For those that decide to share kind words and help, I sincerely appreciate you all, and everybody in my family in Jijiga appreciates and thanks you too. Again, if anybody has any questions or inquiries, please contact me via email by messaging me, or leave me a message on my Facebook and I will respond as soon as the time allows me to. A family friend will be on the ground in Jijiga and will continue to coordinate communication efforts and I will keep everyone concerned updated here on my FaceBook page. Please keep Juweria and her children, my grandmother, my mother, brother, and sister in your prayers as we await further details. I love you all so much.

On Sunday evening, October 30th, our twelve-year-old son was in the backyard with our animals. Out of nowhere, he heard a gunshot, and our cat, Bruce, went running for cover. We searched high and low, looking for him, for hours. Since Bruce doesn't like to leave the yard, we knew he had to be nearby. Finally, we found him hidden under a trailer in a pool of blood, his front leg dangling limply. With tears in our eyes and our hearts racing, we knew he needed help right away if we were going to save him. He was weak and almost lifeless from the shock and blood loss. We immediately rushed him over the hill to the nearest emergency vet (Southern Oregon Veterinary Specialty Center) one and a half hours away. They took him straight into ICU, where they started X-Rays and aggressive life-saving treatments. At around 1 am, the vet explained that Bruce would also require a leg amputation. As if this wasn't enough, he also had extensive injuries from the path of the bullet traveling through his chest. The exit path of the bullet, and fragments of either bullet or bone had lodged elsewhere in his body. After a very long night of waiting, they had him stabilized enough to bring home to our primary vet who was able to do the emergency surgery. Bruce needed an extra day to stabilize enough to endure the amputation surgery. So Bruce spent Monday night in the care of our primary veterinarian. On Tuesday, we were blessed to get the call that the surgery was a success and Bruce would be on his way to making a full recovery. This cat with 8 lives left now, was charming the doctor and staff with his resilience and personality. We were finally able to bring Bruce back home on Wednesday to continue his road to recovery. He is so excited to be home, and wasted no time to be sweet and silly. His purrs and antics are warming our hearts, and just wants one of us to be in constant contact with him. Especially his older kid (16), who he is basically glued to. Bruce is making great strides, but is EXTREMELY upset about having a “cone”, and is constantly figuring out ways to remove it. The whole time we were dealing with the "what happened" and the "what ifs" and so on. The critical care teams were quickly running up bills that our heart could pay, but unfortunately, our wallets could not. We have borrowed beyond what we can repay, and we are reaching out to everyone who knows that you would go to the ends of the earth to save your fur family. We are asking anyone who knows the heartbreak and understands being in over your head, to please donate. We love our cat and are so grateful that he was able to be saved. We appreciate any financial help that you may be able to give. The ER vet = $1,895.82 The Surgery = $2,277.90 Total = $4,173.72

Even though she was on a gurney, when Caera saw us it lit her little face up and she came in wagging. It was at that very moment we knew we would not give up on our girl. Money can be made again and debt can be paid, but Caera is a part of our family and we couldn’t give up on her simply because of the impending financial burden of her treatment. A little bit about Caera’s people...The Acevedo’s. Our names are Alex and Carrie Acevedo, we are both veterans, I was a Marine and Carrie was in the Air Force. On Tuesday, November 8th there was a devastating house fire at Justin’s. His incredibly loved and spoiled two 9-month-old kittens were both in the house; Gus for at least 45 minutes, Frankie for at least 2 hours. Frankie, sadly, was only able to be taken out of the house after he collapsed. A very caring EMT named Donna held both boys with oxygen masks in the back of the ambulance; Gus was foaming at the mouth and Frankie was wheezing, struggling to breathe. Once Justin and his girlfriend arrived, they were able to rush them to Floyd Harbor Animal Hospital, where the boys immediately received more oxygen and an initial assessment that required another urgent ride to East End Veterinary Center. The cost estimate for getting Gus and Frankie the care they needed to survive at East End was a minimum of $10,000; the boys were rushed regardless of the financial cost. They were placed in oxygen cages once they arrived at East End and another assessment revealed Frankie was blind from the smoke, and possible carbon monoxide, inhalation trauma of the fire which deprived his brain of oxygen. The prognosis was guarded, but the boys began receiving the best care they could get: the oxygen cages, IVs of fluids, and nebulizer treatments of medication to help open their airways. Gus (photos above); Frankie (photos below) As of the evening of November 9th, we’re ecstatic to say that the boys continue to improve. Frankie still has a loss of vision but we are all hopeful that more oxygen and nebulizer treatments help him to regain some, or even all, of his vision. They are both breathing comfortably on their own - Gus out of the oxygen cage and Frankie still in the cage - and eating and drinking. Justin and his girlfriend were able to visit the boys in the afternoon and spent time holding them and letting the boys reconnect with eachother as well. We’re very optimistic that the boys will make a full recovery, and we know Frankie will live a very full life with his brother Gus despite not having his complete vision. Justin adores these boys; they have remained his primary concern since the fire happened, and he is doing everything he possibly can to ensure they are the healthiest and happiest cats ever. Absolutely any donation will make a huge difference on the road to getting the boys home and paying off the vet care bill. We sincerely thank you in advance! A HUGE thank you to all the amazing people who have contributed to the boys doing so well: the firefighters that pulled the boys from the house; Donna, for staying with them and giving them the love and oxygen they needed until Justin and his girlfriend arrived; and the wonderful people at Floyd Harbor Animal Hospital and East End Veterinary Center for responding so quickly and effectively to two traumatized kittens, and for being in constant communication to ease the anxiety of the situation. Bela: November is a month where we are incredibly thankful for those we have around us. It couldn’t be more true for me this year. Aj and I were pregnant again and were so excited to be parents thinking no way something bad will happen after the loss we had just suffered two months ago. Unfortunately, this time around would be worse. I got some labs back that right away (thankful to my nursing career) indicated something was wrong. My progesterone was extremely low for me being 6 weeks, and my HCG was very high. I couldn’t get a hold of my OB, which was incredibly frustrating so I made an immediate appointment at a planned parenthood near me. I told them I believed I had an ectopic pregnancy because of my labs and the fact that I was bleeding. They performed a transvaginal ultrasound and, unfortunately, found that the pregnancy was ectopic. The baby was in my right tube. I was sent immediately to the emergency room. Aj and I were immediately admitted and put into a room awaiting further tests. They performed another ultrasound to confirm it and this time it was 3D. I saw the baby’s head forming and the heartbeat . Since the baby had a heartbeat, I had to undergo emergency surgery. The surgeon came in to talk to me about it and told me there was no guarantee he could save my tube. Hearing news like that on top of everything else we had been dealing with was devastating. I consented to the surgery and the risks. I went in for surgery and I was in so much pain when I woke back up. They told me that they did get the pregnancy out of my right tube but went to check on my left tube and found a big mass inside of it. The surgeon doesn’t know if this was a past pregnancy or if this was something more severe like a cancerous mass. The mass on the left was sent to pathology. Aj and I are still awaiting those results. I am currently home in bed. Unfortunately I have dealt with a lot of loss in my life at the age of 24 and one of the things I tend to do now is hold in my emotions but I am trying hard not to do that. I am struggling to sit up and walk without ajs assistance. I am in an enormous amount of pain. More than anything I’m thankful. I am grateful my mom showed me how to be strong & independent at a young age. I am thankful to have a strong man like Aj by my side. I am thankful to have family who is there for me and willing to help me recover. I am thankful to have friends who drop what they have planned to be here for me during this. I am thankful to have a boss who said please take care of yourself first. I am thankful that my surgeon performed a successful surgery. I am hopeful that Aj and I will have a healthy beautiful baby sometime in our future. I am not religious but I do believe that everything happens for a reason. Even though I don’t know the reason, I am confident that with the people I have by my side I will be okay. The mental toll this has taken on me is a big one but I will overcome this. The next three months will be about recovering, healing and listening to my body. As a patient if you feel something is wrong please advocate for yourself. It is imperative. Thank you for your support during this time.
